STEP 1 - Scene: A small mixed green salad (leafy greens with a cherry tomato half and a few bits of dressing or seasoning) on a white square plate. Photographed from above, nearly overhead, with a slight angle.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The white square plate is roughly 24 cm across its side. Treating it as a ~24 cm plate, area ≈ 3.14 x (12)^2 ≈ 452 cm^2. Using the square plate's visible width, the food sits in the central-right portion.

STEP 3 - Items: Mixed leafy greens (green leaf lettuce and red/purple leaves), one cherry tomato (halved, about 3 cm), and small traces of dressing on the plate.

STEP 4 - Area: Mixed leafy greens ~28% of plate area (about 125 cm^2). Cherry tomato ~2% (about 9 cm^2). Dressing/traces ~1%. Total food coverage ~31% of the plate.

STEP 5 - Volume: Leaves: 125 cm^2 x 3 cm (loose, piled) ≈ 375 ml. Tomato: about 9 cm^2 x 2 cm ≈ 18 ml (the tomato is a roughly 3 cm sphere, about 14 ml, so I use ~15 ml).

STEP 6 - Grams: Leaves: 375 ml x 0.15 ≈ 56 g. Tomato: 15 ml x 0.6 ≈ 9 g. Dressing traces: ~2 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Leafy greens ~15 kcal/100 g: 56 g → ~8 kcal. Cherry tomato ~18 kcal/100 g: 9 g → ~2 kcal. Dressing traces ~2 g at ~400 kcal/100 g (oil-based) → ~8 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A modest, lightly dressed side salad with a few leaves and a tomato half of roughly 65–70 g total and about 20 kcal is plausible for what is visible. The plate is not fully covered, so this is well below a full dinner-plate weight.

Total: about 67 g, about 18 kcal (leaves and tomato dominate; the small dressing residue adds a few kcal).
